methodology: Five-verse preliminary screen; independent primary text comparison limited to English Deuteronomy 6:4, 18:15–22 and 1 Corinthians 8:4–6; Quran 12:109 directly retrieved, remaining verse readings require independent textual verification. Not a comprehensive tradition survey.

assessments.subject: Belief mixed with association of partners
assessments.evidence: Deuteronomy affirms one God; Paul discusses idols and one God while articulating a distinctive Christological formulation. Neither reproduces the Qur'anic claim that many believers also associate partners.

assessments.subject: Warning of sudden punishment or the Hour
assessments.evidence: Broad eschatological warning; no specific pre-Islamic source locator checked for this verse.

assessments.subject: Invitation to God with insight; denial of association
assessments.evidence: Both affirm exclusive devotion to one God, but the Qur'an speaks in the first-person prophetic invitation with insight, unlike Israel's covenantal confession.

assessments.subject: Earlier human messengers, ruined communities, hereafter
assessments.evidence: Deuteronomy describes a prophet raised from Israel and criteria for prophetic speech; Qur'an generalizes earlier inspired men from settlements and calls for travel to observe ruined peoples.

assessments.subject: Messengers' despair and divine rescue
assessments.evidence: The sequence of despair, rescue and punishment warrants further comparative research; no precise source has been checked in this pass.

dossier.title: Monotheism, prophetic proclamation and judgment in Yusuf's epilogue
dossier.comparative_summary: 12:106–110 moves beyond Joseph's narrative to shared and divergent monotheistic, prophetic and eschatological themes. Deuteronomy 6:4 is an exclusive-monotheism thematic comparison; Deuteronomy 18:15–22 provides a different, Israel-centered institution of prophecy. 1 Corinthians 8:4–6 discusses idols and one God but has distinctive Christian language about Jesus Christ.
dossier.chronology: The biblical works are pre-Islamic compositions; precise composition strata and extant manuscript dates must be distinguished and documented before publication.
